events.name: Inauguration of ACE & Guest Lecture on Cyber Security: How Hackers Actually Hack!!
events.description: ACE kicked off the 2024-25 academic year with its formal inauguration ceremony followed by a guest lecture on cybersecurity. Chief guest Mr. Sriram Kesavan, Founder and Director of Security at TG Cyberlabs-Secufra Labs, spoke on how hackers actually exploit systems, covering types of hacking and practical, real-world attack methods. The event also featured a badge distribution ceremony for new office bearers and a recap video of ACE's 2023-24 activities.

events.name: Quiz ACE 'C' Edition
events.description: An online C programming quiz open to all years of the CSE and AI&DS departments, held via Quizizz between 7:00 PM and 7:30 PM. The quiz was designed to reinforce fundamental C concepts and encourage healthy academic competition, with each participant allowed a single attempt on a stable connection. The report's reflection section refers to it once as the 'Data Structures Edition' and dates it to October 19th, which conflicts with the title page's 14th October date - likely an OCR/report inconsistency.
events.prizes: Exciting prizes for leaderboard toppers (no specific amount stated)
events.requirements: Single attempt only per participant; join via provided game link/code; name format required as Name_Department_Year_Rollno; portal closed strictly at 7:30 PM.

events.name: Tech Debate
events.description: A structured debate tournament on current and emerging technology topics such as AI ethics, ChatGPT in education, autonomous vehicles, and the impact of mobile phones on society. Twelve teams competed through preliminary, quarterfinal, and semifinal rounds before two teams met in the final. The event aimed to sharpen participants' critical thinking, communication, and argumentation skills in a competitive setting.

events.name: Women Who Pitch
events.description: A Women's Day event giving female students a platform to pitch business/tech ideas with confidence and creativity. Teams randomly drew a pitch topic and presented within three to five minutes, judged on feasibility, innovation, and cost-effectiveness, followed by a Q&A with judges. The event covered a mix of technology-focused and sustainable business ideas.

events.name: Interrupt'25
events.venue: Library Seminar Hall (inauguration & valedictory); 5th Block Classrooms and CS Labs (competition events)
events.description: ACE's flagship National Level Technical Symposium, bringing together students from multiple colleges for a day of technical competitions and a workshop across the 5th Block. The symposium was inaugurated by chief guest Mr. R Soorya Prakash (SVCE alumnus and Software Engineer II - Machine Learning at Kaleris), who spoke on understanding and utilizing LLMs, and closed with a valedictory ceremony where prizes and certificates were distributed by the HoD, Dr. R. Anitha. It comprised nine individual sub-events spanning coding, design, data analysis, paper presentation, and an AR workshop.

events.name: The Lost Code
events.description: A coding competition for participants who thrive under pressure, combining debugging, logic reconstruction, and algorithmic problem-solving. Participants worked through fragmented, error-riddled code across multiple rounds of increasing difficulty, culminating in a real-time coding duel in the final stage.

events.name: Code Bingo
events.description: A coding and cryptography challenge that began with a Cryptography & Binary Encoding Quiz testing participants' decoding and encryption skills under time pressure. The top 10 teams advanced to a 'Code Bingo' showdown, racing to solve coding problems and complete a valid Bingo pattern to be crowned champions.

events.name: Conquer and Design
events.description: A design-focused competition challenging participants to solve a given design problem in real time, balancing functionality, aesthetics, and efficiency while justifying their choices. The event rewarded creativity, strategic planning, and on-the-spot adaptability.

events.name: Gauntlet Quest
events.description: A multi-stage coding and problem-solving competition themed around collecting 'Infinity Stones' by solving coding challenges under time pressure. Teams that gathered the most stones gained advantages heading into a final round with real-world company challenges requiring innovative solutions using cutting-edge technologies.

events.name: Uno Mania
events.description: A two-round event blending UNO, coding, and strategy. Round 1 was a technical crossword-style puzzle solved for speed, with the top 12 teams advancing; Round 2 had teams draw UNO cards introducing tasks, penalties, or advantages while solving three coding problems under time pressure.

events.name: Squid Game
events.description: A solo, elimination-based event combining intellect, strategy, and survival instincts across multiple challenges, including precision tasks, a high-pressure 'Red Light, Green Light' puzzle round, and a fate-based dice roll determining the final challenge.

events.name: Tech Connex
events.description: A two-round event testing problem-solving, analytical thinking, and data visualization skills. Round 1, 'Connexion', had teams decipher hidden connections between technology-related images, words, and clues; Round 2, 'Data Warriors', had finalists analyze a mystery dataset in Power BI and present insights within 60 minutes.

events.name: A Hands-On Workshop on Exploring Augmented Reality
events.description: A hands-on augmented reality (AR) workshop conducted by industry professional Ms. Kavitha Chandan from VyVoxel. Participants were introduced to AR fundamentals and the Unity game engine, learning to implement marker-based and marker-less AR applications.

events.name: Biz Prompt
events.date: 6th & 8th April 2025 (title page lists 8th April 2025; reflection report states '8th March 2025', likely a typo)
events.description: A two-phase tech-business event, 'BizPrompt Challenge', exclusively for 2nd and 3rd year CSE and AI&DS students. Phase 1 was a 30-minute online quiz on web development, UI/UX, and business thinking that shortlisted the top 15 teams; Phase 2 had finalists build and pitch a web-based product solution using AI tools and modern design principles.
events.participants: Top 15 teams shortlisted from Phase 1 online prelims
events.prizes: Participation certificates for all; prizes and recognition awarded to top-performing teams (specific amounts not stated)
